params.body:
Reports were the one kind of content the Studio never saw. The calendar lived in
a seeder on the public site and the PDF arrived through an artisan command over
ssh, so the two decisions that are actually editorial (when a report goes out,
and how much anyone may read without paying) both needed a developer.

Needs Trendwolves/gentells-pipeline#177, which holds the shelf and does the
rendering.

## The shelf

Maarten's year as he writes it, and per row what has really landed. That second
label is **derived, never typed**: the announced status runs ahead of reality on
purpose, and R2 stood at "available, with preview" for weeks with no PDF and no
pages. A row reads `announced` until a file is actually there.

Opening a row gives the calendar fields, an upload with a count of pages to
leave open, and the rendered pages themselves. Only those pages are turned into
images on the far side, so a preview here is a picture and never the PDF with a
lid on it.

## Two details worth knowing

The preview images are fetched as blobs rather than dropped in an `img src`:
that route is behind staff auth and an image request carries no `Authorization`
header. Opening it up would be simpler and is exactly what must not happen,
because a report that is not out yet is not out yet.

The palette, eyebrow and button moved to `style.js` rather than being copied. A
second copy of a palette is how two screens of one product drift apart a hex at
a time. The report hooks sit in `hooks.js` next to the article ones.
params.title: A reports shelf: the year, and which of it has landed
